blocks.passage:
Meetings, done well, are one of the most useful tools in business. Done badly, they are where time goes to die. The difference is not the topic — it is the chair.

A good chairperson does three things consistently. They share a clear agenda in advance, so everyone arrives prepared. They protect the time, gently interrupting when a topic drifts too far. And, crucially, they close with decisions and owners — never "let's think about it" without naming who is going to think, by when, and bring what back.

The test of a meeting is not how many people spoke or how long it lasted. It is whether anyone, one week later, can describe what was decided and who is doing what.

items.q: According to the text, what makes the difference between a good and a bad meeting?
items.why: "The difference is not the topic — it is the chair."

items.q: Why does a good chairperson share the agenda in advance?
items.why: "They share a clear agenda in advance, so everyone arrives prepared."

items.q: What does the text say a meeting should close with?
items.why: "they close with decisions and owners" — nomeando quem faz o quê e até quando.

items.q: The text criticises "let's think about it" because it…
options: names no owner, deadline or deliverable
items.why: Inferência: sem nomear quem pensa, até quando e o que traz de volta, a frase não gera ação.

items.q: What, according to the text, is the real test of a meeting?
options: Whether people remember the decisions a week later
items.why: "whether anyone, one week later, can describe what was decided and who is doing what."

audio.text:
Right, thanks everyone for being on time. We've got thirty minutes and three topics, so I'll keep us moving.

First, the budget. Last month we reviewed the forecast and we agreed to hold spending until Q3. Since then, nothing has changed on that front, so I'd like to confirm we're still holding — Priya, can you own the follow-up with finance and report back by Friday?

Second, the launch date. I know this could run long, so let's park the detail and just decide the date today. We've discussed the options twice already. My proposal is the fourteenth. Any objections? No? Good, the fourteenth it is.

Third, hiring. This one has drifted in every meeting, so I want a decision, not a discussion. Tom, you'll draft the job description and share it by Wednesday. That's an action item, not a maybe.

We're at twenty-six minutes. Let me wrap up: budget held, Priya following up; launch on the fourteenth; Tom on the job description by Wednesday. Thanks all.

items.q: How does Oliver open the meeting?
options: By noting the time limit and number of topics
By reading the full agenda aloud
items.why: "We've got thirty minutes and three topics, so I'll keep us moving."

items.q: What was decided about the budget?
items.why: "we agreed to hold spending until Q3… I'd like to confirm we're still holding."

items.q: Why does Oliver "park the detail" on the launch date?
options: Because it could make the topic run long
items.why: "I know this could run long, so let's park the detail and just decide the date today."

items.q: How does Oliver handle the hiring topic differently?
options: He removes it from the agenda
He asks for a decision, not a discussion, and assigns an owner
items.why: "I want a decision, not a discussion. Tom, you'll draft the job description… That's an action item, not a maybe."

items.q: What does Oliver do at twenty-six minutes?
options: Wraps up by restating the decisions and owners
items.why: "Let me wrap up: budget held, Priya following up; launch on the fourteenth; Tom on the job description by Wednesday."

items.q: "Sofia will **chair** the steering committee this quarter." To chair a meeting means to…
items.why: To chair = presidir, conduzir a reunião.

items.q: "The discussion started to **drift**, so he brought it back to the agenda." To drift means to…
items.why: To drift = desviar do assunto.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Could you circulate the ___ so everyone knows what we'll cover?"
items.why: Agenda = pauta, enviada antes; minutes (ata) é o registro do que aconteceu.

items.q: The **minutes** of a meeting are…
options: the written record of what was discussed and decided
items.why: Minutes = ata; o registro do que foi discutido e decidido.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Let's ___ — we're out of time. Priya owns the follow-up."
items.why: To wrap up = concluir, encerrar.

items.q: "Can we **circle back to** the budget after lunch?" To circle back to means to…
items.why: Circle back to = voltar a um assunto mais tarde.

items.q: "Sorry to **jump in**, but I have a quick point." To jump in means to…
items.why: Jump in = entrar na conversa, muitas vezes interrompendo brevemente.

items.q: "Let's **move on** — we've covered this." To move on means to…
items.why: Move on = passar ao próximo ponto.

items.q: "I'll **follow up** with finance and report back." To follow up means to…
options: take further action after the meeting
items.why: Follow up = dar sequência, tomar a ação seguinte.

items.q: "We're **running over** — let's keep the last point short." To run over means to…
items.why: Run over = passar do tempo previsto.
